deadline.value: Chancellor's Scholarship (the University scheme open to international students): Dec 7, 2026. Funded-project deadlines: Astronomy Nov 16, 2026 and Feb 2, 2027; Condensed Matter and Theory Jan 20, 2027; Particle Physics Jan 22, 2027; late releases for Condensed Matter/Theory Mar 5 and Mar 18, 2027. Visa-requiring applicants for Sep/Oct 2027 must apply by Aug 2, 2027.
deadline.quote: Apply by these dates to be considered for funded places: | Warwick's Postgraduate Chancellors Scholarship December 7th 2026 | Nov 16th 2026 and Feb 2nd 2027 | Condensed Matter Physics: 20th January 2027 | Elementary Particle Physics: 22nd January 2027 | Theoretical Physics: 20th January 2027 | Collaborative projects: March 5th 2027 | General projects: March 18th 2027

also.quote: For research courses that start in September and October 2027, the application deadline for students who require a visa to study in the UK is 2 August 2027.

supervisor.value: The department encourages emailing potential supervisors of projects that interest you; list project titles and supervisors in the proposal section. The University-wide guide advises securing a supervisor before applying.
supervisor.quote: We encourage you to email potential supervisors in projects that interest you | Put the project title(s) and the associated supervisor(s) in the proposal section of the application; a detailed proposal is not required

also.quote: We advise you to make contact with and secure a supervisor before you apply.

funding.value: Funded projects pay fees and a stipend, but in most cases are limited to UK nationals; a proportion are funded for international students. The Chancellor's Scholarship (home or overseas fees plus stipend for 3.5 years) is competitive.
funding.quote: In most cases the funding for these projects are limited to UK nationals. | However, a proportion of some of these projects are funded for international students. | Warwick's Chancellors Scholarship is a competitive scheme run by the University to fund both UK and international postgraduate research students.

entry_route.value: Minimum is a 2:1 BSc honours, MSci or MPhys (or international equivalent) in physics or a related subject, but competitive projects and funding typically go to first-class MSci/MPhys-level applicants.
entry_route.quote: The minimum requirements are an upper second-class BSc honours, MSci or MPhys degree, or international equivalent, in Physics or a related subject. | Competitive projects and funding sources will typically go to students with an MSci or MPhys level degree and first-class honours (or equivalent).

app_fee.value: No application fee for postgraduate research applications (the £75 fee applies to taught courses)
app_fee.quote: There is no application fee for postgraduate research applications or Postgraduate Awards (PGAs).

fee_waiver.quote: There is no application fee for postgraduate research applications or Postgraduate Awards (PGAs).

toefl_min.value: Physics PhD is English Band A. TOEFL iBT before Jan 21, 2026: 92 (R22, L21, S23, W21); on or after Jan 21, 2026: 4.5 total with at least 4.5 in each component. IELTS 6.5 with no component below 6.0.
toefl_min.quote: Band A | 92, comprising Reading 22, Listening 21, Speaking 23, Writing 21 | Total Score 4.5 including minimum of 4.5 in each component

also.quote: Band A | IELTS overall score of 6.5, minimum component scores not below 6.0

english_waiver.value: A test can be waived only for nationals of a UKVI-recognised English-speaking country, or for a degree taught entirely in English in such a country (completed within 2 years 4 months of the start), at the department's discretion. India is not on the UKVI list, and the India country page lists no exemption.
english_waiver.quote: You are a national of an English speaking country recognised by UK Visa & Immigration (UKVI) | You have been educated entirely in English, in a UK Visa & Immigration (UKVI) recognised English speaking country, for the duration of your degree and completed this qualification within the last 2 years and 4 months before the start date of your course.

notes: No research proposal is needed for physics; name advertised projects and supervisors instead. Shortlisted applicants are interviewed (Condensed Matter/Theory in-person day Jan 20, 2027; Particle Physics Feb 10, 2027).
